column1: # The X11 libraries Qt's xcb platform plugin (libQt6XcbQpa, and libxcb-glx for its GLX integration) needs and a fresh desktop install may lack: the usual
# "could not load the Qt platform plugin xcb" error. stage.sh puts them beside the Qt libraries, where the plugin's RUNPATH ($ORIGIN) finds them. They come from
# Ubuntu 22.04's archive, so their glibc needs stay under DroidPlay's floor (2.34); libxcb.so.1 itself, which every X11 system has, comes from the system.
# libxkbcommon comes with libxkbcommon-x11, of the same version: -x11 uses libxkbcommon's internals (Debian pins the pair to one version), and Ubuntu's
# 1.4.0 -x11 beside Fedora 44's libxkbcommon 1.13 crashed in xkb_x11_state_new_from_device as Qt's xcb plugin connected. Every Qt library then takes the
# bundled libxkbcommon, which reads the system's keyboard layouts (/usr/share/X11/xkb) as any version does.
# Each row: the package, its file under https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/, its SHA-256 (from jammy's Packages index).
